thread.title: 5G Wireless Top Stock Picks Include These Below-The-Radar Companies |

author: REINHARDT KRAUSE
title: 5G Wireless Top Stock Picks Include These Below-The-Radar Companies |
text:
AT&T ( T ), Verizon Communications ( VZ ) and network gear makers LM Ericsson ( ERICY ) and Nokia ( NOK ) are among Goldman Sachs' top stock picks in a global report on the rollout of 5G wireless services.
X Telecom gear makers Ciena ( CIEN ) and Adtran ( ADTN ) also stand to benefit from the launch of 5G wireless, says Goldman Sachs in the 5G report, published on Monday.
"In the U.S., we identify Verizon, AT&T, Adtran, Ciena, Lumentum Holdings ( LITE ), Corning ( GLW ), CommScope Holding ( COMM ), Keysight Technologies ( KEYS ), Xilinx ( XLNX ) and Analog Devices ( ADI ) as key beneficiaries of 5G, while we expect Juniper Networks ( JNPR ) and Belden ( BDC ) to face headwinds in their carrier focused segments," the report said.
Xilinx makes programmable chips for prototype 5G wireless gear. Keysight makes testing equipment. Ciena, Lumentum and Corning provide fiber-optic technology.
 Verizon is testing 5G wireless for delivering high-speed internet services to residential homes, mainly in apartment buildings. Verizon's new CEO, Hans Vestberg, is a former chief executive of Sweden-based Ericsson.
At an analysts meeting last week, AT&T said it's more focused on providing private, high-speed 5G services to companies for commercial purposes.
Apple To Hold Off On 5G iPhones Goldman Sachs doesn't expect 5G smartphones to be available until 2020. Apple ( AAPL ), meanwhile, will not make iPhones that can access 5G networks until 2020 or later, Bloomberg reported on Monday.
Apple tends to wait until next-generation wireless networks are widely available before equipping iPhones with new chips. In the 5G generation, Apple's plans could create an opening for rival Samsung, analysts say.
"We expect 2019 to be the first year that 5G technology sees material deployment with a focus on fixed wireless broadband in the home," said the Goldman Sachs report. "Following this, we expect 5G cellular rollouts for smartphones usage to accelerate in 2020 to accompany the availability of mass market handsets."
In urban areas, 5G wireless networks will require new "small-cell" radio antennas. The small-cell antennas — hung on utility poles or building rooftops — will connect to fiber-optic wiring at local hubs. Mini data centers in neighborhoods, in turn, will link to cloud-computing infrastructure. Nokia and Ericsson are developing 5G cloud gateways.
Pundits see self-driving cars, smart urban infrastructure and drones as big users.
S&P Global Ratings in October issued a cautious report on the rollout of 5G services. Wireless firms could wait five to 10 years for a payback on investments, said the credit-rating agency.
